method: Use the traditional evenly increased flat-circle sequence: round 1 contains S stitches in the starting ring, and every later round adds S stitches. Round R therefore contains S×R stitches; the complete project works S×R×(R+1)/2 stitches including round 1. Round 2 places two stitches in every earlier stitch. From round 3 onward, each of S repeats places two stitches in the next stitch followed by one stitch in each of R−2 stitches, consuming S×(R−1) earlier stitches and producing S×R. Gauge is measured on a flat swatch over 10 cm or 4 in. The geometric model gives each round one measured round-height of radius: radius = rounds×gauge span/round gauge, diameter = 2×radius, and circumference = pi×diameter. Circumference divided by final stitches is the edge stitch pitch; gauge span divided by stitch gauge is the swatch stitch width. Their signed percentage difference is 100×(edge pitch/swatch pitch−1). Starting stitches are whole numbers 3–24, total rounds 1–40 and both gauge counts decimals 1–100; blank, negative, exponent and malformed values are refused. Dimensions and pitches are rounded half-up to four decimals and the percentage to two. The estimate assumes even flat rounds and excludes stitch type, yarn, hook, shaping stagger and drape. All computation is local; nothing is stored or requested.

sources.title: Shelley Husband Crochet: published 6- and 12-start flat-circle sequences add the starting count each round.
